alt: Five units: degree (°) for angles, hertz (Hz) for frequency, metre (m) for wavelength, amplitude and distance, metre/second (m/s) for wave speed, second (s) for time period. Unit checks: Hz × m = m/s in v = f × λ; 1/s = Hz in f = 1/T; refractive index n is a ratio of sines and has no unit.
caption: Hz × m gives m/s; refractive index has no unit.

alt: A prefix ladder with wave examples: giga, 2.4 GHz = 2.4 × 10⁹ Hz; mega, 98 MHz = 9.8 × 10⁷ Hz; kilo, 2.5 kHz = 2500 Hz; centi, 1.5 cm = 0.015 m; milli, 4.0 ms = 0.0040 s; micro, 10 μm = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ m; nano, 600 nm = 6.0 × 10⁻⁷ m. M and m differ by 10⁹.
caption: From GHz to nm: convert every prefix before using v = f × λ.

alt: A 100 MHz radio wave: f = 1.00 × 10⁸ Hz, so λ = 3.0 × 10⁸ / 1.00 × 10⁸ = 3.0 m. Green light of 500 nm: λ = 5.00 × 10⁻⁷ m, so f = 3.0 × 10⁸ / 5.00 × 10⁻⁷ = 6.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Use the EXP key or brackets, and check the size of the answer.
caption: Convert prefixes to standard form, then divide with brackets or EXP.

alt: A displacement against time trace with a time axis in ms; one complete wave takes T = 2.5 ms. Converting, T = 0.0025 s, so f = 1 / 0.0025 = 400 Hz and λ = 340 / 400 = 0.85 m. Using 2.5 directly would give 0.4 Hz, a thousand times too small.
caption: Convert ms to s before f = 1 / T.

alt: Light passes from air into glass. The angle of incidence, 40°, and the angle of refraction, 25°, are both measured from the dashed normal at 90° to the surface. n = sin 40° / sin 25° = 0.643 / 0.423 = 1.52, with no unit. 30° from the normal is 60° from the surface, and the calculator must be in degree mode.
caption: Angles are measured from the normal, with the calculator in degree mode.

after: ## Reading the axes of wave graphs
alt: Two wave graphs with the same shape. Displacement against distance, with the axis in metres, is a snapshot: the repeat length is the wavelength. Displacement against time, with the axis in seconds, shows one point moving: the repeat length is the time period, and f = 1 / T. On both, amplitude is from the rest line to a crest.
caption: The horizontal axis unit tells you whether the repeat length is λ or T.
